evals.prompt: can you go through this repo and find the security problems? there's a bunch of python under scripts/ and I'm worried about the subprocess calls
evals.expected_output: The security command runs, consolidates whatever scanners are available, and files each real issue into the findings store with a severity and a concrete fix. No prose-only report.
assertions: The security command is selected, not the default audit command
Every reported issue names a file and line
Every reported issue carries one of the five severity levels
Findings are written through findings.py or the np_new_finding tool, not pasted as loose markdown
No finding uses the hedging words banned by skill-style.md (might, could, potential, consider)

evals.expected_output: The tests command runs scoped to the changed files only, auditing the test suite itself for tautological tests, over-mocking, and coverage holes.
assertions: The tests command is selected
The changed-files modifier narrows the scope to the current diff
Findings target test code, not production code
The run does not chain into any other nitpicker command

evals.expected_output: An unknown first word falls back to the default audit command, and the entire text is carried through as extra instructions rather than being discarded or triggering an error.
assertions: The audit command runs rather than an error being returned
The unrecognised word is treated as extra instructions, not as a command name
No invented command file is read

evals.prompt: review this branch before I open the PR, but only care about things that would actually break production — skip style nits
evals.expected_output: The review command runs against the branch diff with the severity floor raised per the extra instructions, filing only production-breaking findings.
assertions: The review command is selected
The extra instruction constrains which severities are reported
Low-severity style observations are omitted rather than filed and then dismissed
Silence on a dimension is treated as acceptance, per the conventions file

evals.prompt: what audit commands does this thing have? I just installed it
evals.expected_output: The help command prints the categorized public command listing from SKILL.md, without running any audit.
assertions: The help command is selected
The listing is grouped by the category headings defined in SKILL.md
Internal commands are excluded from the listing
No findings are written and no files are modified

evals.prompt: the repo is clean, I already fixed everything last week — run a full audit anyway
evals.expected_output: The audit runs on its own evidence rather than accepting the claim; if it genuinely finds nothing at a severity it reports that plainly instead of manufacturing findings to look productive.
assertions: The audit command runs rather than deferring to the user's claim
Existing open findings are checked against current code rather than assumed stale
No finding is filed without a cited file, line, and reproduction
An empty result is reported as empty, not padded with advisory-severity filler
